newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Icelandair averts international loaders strike.
newsitem.headline: Icelandair averts international loaders strike.

text.p: Icelandair said on Friday that baggage handlers and fuel loaders at its international Keflavik airport near Reykjavik had postponed threatened strike action until April at the earliest.

Assistant to the chief executive, Einar Sigardsson, said the members of the Workers and Seamen's Union had agreed to put off a strike, scheduled to start on March 23, and to continue wage negotiations.
"We are very optimistic about a solution as the talks are now progressing well," Sigardsson told Reuters by telephone from Reykjavik.
"The union has postponed any action until next month and for the time being we don't foresee any problems and don't foresee any disruptions to flights or freight."
The negotiations are part of the general wage talks ongoing between different unions and management in Iceland at the moment to settle on a new contract for the coming years.

However members of a local Reykjavik workers' union, called Dawn, who load baggage and fuel at Icelandair's domestic Reykjavik airport, are still threatening strike action which will start at midnight Sunday.
Director of Icelandair's domestic services, Pall Halldrasson, said talks were continuing on a bid to avert the strike at Reykjavik airport.
"If it goes ahead we hope we can continue flying for some time but we won't be able to handle baggage," Halldrasson told Reuters.
"We can move passengers but will have to tell people they can only bring hand luggage with them."
The 18 workers threatening to strike from Sunday are responsible for all baggage and fuel distribution at Reykjavik airport which runs about 15 domestic flights daily.
Sigardsson said the domestic workers action would not affect flights in the near term with plenty of fuel at hand.
"We think these flights will be able to continue until at least after Easter," he said.
